method: Reviewed the full 2024 article PDF retrieved from DergiPark, comparing the article-level journal-page license badge with the 2024 issue licensing text and the journal-wide policy. The DLSU-D OPAC entry point was also attempted; it redirected to a site-selection page, so the cited 2018 thesis record could not be independently searched there. A temporary source-review copy remains outside the repository; no thesis text, article-derived tables, or source geometry were added.

sampling.collectionPeriod: April 2023 (dry season, as reported by authors)
sampling.collectionMethod: Haphazard and random seine-net collection, as reported by the authors.
sampling.taxonomyLimit: The authors deliberately report Tilapia sp. because of possible interspecific hybridization and limited specificity of the feral fish gene pool. Do not resolve these samples to Oreochromis niloticus or another species from this paper.
sampling.dataAvailability: The article says its data will be made available on request; no request was sent.

reuse.articlePage: The article record displays a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 badge.
reuse.journalPolicy: The 2024 issue licensing text and journal-wide publication policy state CC BY 4.0.
reuse.articlePdf: The reviewed PDF identifies author copyright but does not state a license in its text layer.
reuse.decision: Do not reuse article-derived coordinates or other article content in public app data until the publisher confirms the item-specific license. Citation and short factual bibliographic metadata are retained internally.

limitations: The article documents a single April 2023 juvenile-fish sampling campaign, not current presence, abundance, catchability, safety, diet, fishing legality, or a complete river checklist.
The study supports only genus-rank Tilapia sp.; it does not independently confirm the species-level Oreochromis niloticus claim in the separate 2019 paper.
The station coordinates locate the study sampling sites and do not delineate the whole river or establish access.
The article page and journal-wide license statements conflict; article-specific reuse remains unverified.
nextAction: Keep the species-level Maragondon tilapia claim held. Ask the journal/publisher to clarify the article-specific license and pursue the cited DLSU-D thesis through its library route only if record-level access is needed; do not send requests without explicit authorization.
